d: Explains Roblox groups and how to collaborate with multiple creators on the same game.
h:
A Roblox group allows multiple creators to work on the same game, use the same assets, share profits, and give credit to all contributors.

Group ownership of games helps creators collaborate and operate as independent studios. If a conflict arises within a group, Roblox cannot help arbitrate or resolve disagreements.

Group creation

Creating a group costs 100 Robux. You can manage its roles and permissions from the Creator Dashboard or Communities.

Before creating a group, carefully read through the rules and expectations for group management.

To create a new group:

  1. Navigate to the Creator Dashboard, expand the account switcher in the upper‑left, and click the plus (+) button.
  2. On the Create Group page, upload an image for the group logo and enter the group name.
  3. When ready, click the Purchase button. Once the group is created, you'll be directed to the group profile page where you can modify the group's details, including adding up to three social links.

Roles and permissions

Group members can be assigned one or multiple roles within a group, and each role has permissions which specify the abilities of its members.

Role configuration is only accessible if you're the group owner or you have permission to create, configure, and assign group roles.

To manage group role assignments programmatically from a game server, use HttpService to call the supported Open Cloud Groups endpoints. For setup and sample code, see Use with Open Cloud.

  1. From the Creator Dashboard, expand the account switcher in the upper‑left and select the group.
  2. Expand the account switcher again and select Roles.
  3. For each role, carefully confirm the permissions under the **** tab.

Permissions are organized into *, , and *** categories. The sections below describe the permissions available in each category.

### Community

  1. IMPORTANT Click the **** button to apply the permission settings.
  2. OPTIONAL Click the * tab and choose a color and visibility setting for the role, then click the * button.
A role's **** section is also where group owners and members with sufficient permissions can remove a role entirely through the **Delete Role** button.

Roles are listed in hierarchy order: a role higher in the list has more authority than a role below it. This order matters because some permissions only let members manage roles below their own highest role.

Each role is either public or private. Public roles can be shown on a Community page and in experiences. Private roles are shown only on role and permission management surfaces to authorized members, or to members who hold the private role. Visibility changes where a role appears; it doesn't change the permissions the role grants.

To grant *, , , , or ***, you must have two-step verification enabled.

Manage members

Member configuration is only accessible if you're the group owner or you have permission to manage other members and their roles.

To manage members from the Creator Dashboard:

  1. Expand the account switcher in the upper-left and select the group.
  2. Expand the account switcher again and select ****.
  3. Use the Member tab to search for existing members or filter them by role. Use the Invited tab to review pending invitations.

To add a member, click the **** button and search for their username. Roblox notifies invited creators according to their notification preferences. You can also copy the group link and share it directly.

Manage roles

You can manage role assignments from either the **** page or a specific role:

  • On the * page, click the *plus (+) button next to a member to open the role menu. To assign a role, click the plus (+) button next to it under Add roles. To unassign a role, click the minus (-) button next to it under Current roles, or click the × button on an assigned role next to the member's name.
  • On the Roles page, select a role and open its * tab. Click the button to search for group members and assign them to the role. To unassign a member, click the minus (-)* button at the end of their row.

Member removal

To remove a member from the group, click the ⋮ button at the end of their row, select Kick user, and confirm the action.

Manage payouts

If you're the group owner or you have the correct permission within Group Revenue, you'll find a Payouts page under Finances in the left navigation. Here, you can send one‑time payouts, as well as define percentage splits with other members.

Some groups may not have this page unlocked initially for various reasons, such as the age of the group or insufficient funds to payout.

Payouts cannot be shared across group members for games that charge for paid access in local currency.

One-time payouts

One-time payouts can be made to members in a batch, selecting a set amount for each. Safety features include 2FA challenges, confirmation dialogues, and checks around the eligibility of members being paid.

Once you click the Send Robux button, you can choose payout recipients from the popup or upload a .csv spreadsheet file with the columns userId and payoutInRobux, for example:

Recurring payouts

Recurring payouts can also be made across the entire group and per‑game, assigning a percentage payout to each member before the remainder enters the group's overall balance.

Consider the following scenario where a group game Laser Maze is split 40%–30%–10% among three members, with a remainder of 20%.


<div class="gcell" markdown="1"><img src="../assets/misc/Box-Label-A.png" width="40" />

<div class="gcell" markdown="1">
Assuming the game earns 1000 Robux, the three members receive 400, 300, and 100 Robux respectively (40%–30%–10%).
</div>

<div class="gcell" markdown="1"><img src="../assets/misc/Box-Label-B.png" width="40" />

<div class="gcell" markdown="1">
The remaining 200 Robux (20% of the game split) passes onward to the **group split** percentages, defined at 20%–20%–10% among the same three members; they receive an additional 40, 40, and 20 Robux respectively.
</div>

<div class="gcell" markdown="1"><img src="../assets/misc/Box-Label-C.png" width="40" />

<div class="gcell" markdown="1">
The remaining 100 Robux (50% of the group split) is placed in the group's overall balance.
</div>

Note that revenue from private server subscriptions does not change if you adjust split percentages at a later time, meaning that if a player buys a private server subscription, the split percentages at time of purchase will apply to that particular subscription forever (until it is canceled). This policy may be changed in the future.

Group audit logs

Group members with the **** permission can review group changes using these group management surfaces:

  • On the Creator Dashboard, select Activity History under Collaboration.
  • On Communities, open the community's configuration page and select Audit Log.

Group owners can use these logs to monitor activity that might violate group guidelines.

Intellectual property protection

Group members with permission to edit all group games can enable the Place Copying setting for a creation, potentially allowing the entire Roblox community to copy it and use assets within it. To help protect intellectual property in a group, the owner or members with sufficient permissions should:

  • Confirm that each member is assigned the appropriate role.
  • Check that each group role has the correct permissions.
  • Confirm that the Place Copying setting is disabled before private assets are added.

kid.simple: A Roblox group is a team account that lets several creators work on the same games, share assets, split the money the games earn, and all get credit. This page explains how to create a group, how roles and permissions decide what each member can do, how to invite and remove members, how to pay members, and how to protect your work. Setting this up carefully matters, because Roblox cannot step in to settle arguments inside a group.
kid.analogy: A group is like a school club. The club has officers (roles) such as president, treasurer, and member. Each officer has certain jobs they are allowed to do (permissions), and the treasurer decides how the money from the bake sale gets shared.
keyPoints: Creating a group costs 100 Robux. On the Creator Dashboard, open the account switcher in the top-left, click the plus (+) button, add a logo and name, and click Purchase.
Members get one or more roles, and each role has permissions, such as playing unreleased games, editing games, publishing games, or managing money.
Roles are listed from highest to lowest. Some permissions only let you manage people whose highest role is below yours.
Click Save after changing a role's permissions, or nothing changes. Some powerful permissions require you to have two-step verification turned on.
Invite members from the Members page, assign or remove roles with the plus and minus buttons, and kick members from the three-dot menu.
Under Finances > Payouts, you can send one-time Robux payments or set recurring percentage splits.

Example split: a game earns 1000 Robux, split 40%, 30%, 10%. Members get 400, 300, and 100. The leftover 200 goes to the group split of 20%, 20%, 10%, giving 40, 40, and 20 more, and 100 stays in the group.
Members who can edit all games can turn on Place Copying, so check roles carefully and keep copying off to protect your work.

terms.group: A shared account that can own games, assets, and Robux, with many members working together. Roblox also calls these communities.
terms.role: A rank or job title in the group, like Owner, Developer, or Tester.
terms.permission: Something a role is allowed to do, like edit games or send payouts.
terms.hierarchy: The order of roles from most powerful to least. A higher role can manage roles below it, but not above.
terms.public vs private role: A public role can be shown on the community page and in games. A private role is only shown to people who manage roles or who have that role.
terms.two-step verification (2FA): An extra login check, like a code, on top of your password.
terms.payout: Sending Robux from the group to a member.
terms.recurring payout: An automatic percentage of earnings sent to members every time the game earns, instead of one manual payment.
terms.split: Dividing earnings by percentages. 40% of 1000 Robux is 400 Robux.
terms.remainder: What is left after the splits. If members get 40% + 30% + 10% = 80%, the remainder is 20%.
terms.CSV: A simple spreadsheet file. For bulk payouts, it has columns `userId` and `payoutInRobux`.
terms.audit log: A history list of changes made in the group, so owners can see who did what.
terms.intellectual property: Your original creations, like your game's scripts, models, and art, which belong to you or the group.

watchOut: Giving new members powerful roles like publishing or managing revenue right away. Start with less and add more once you trust them.
Forgetting to click Save after changing permissions.
Expecting Roblox support to fix a fight in your group. Roblox cannot settle group disagreements, so agree on rules and money splits early.
Changing split percentages and expecting old private server subscriptions to change too. They keep the split from when they were bought.
